# Architecture & Technical Foundation

## SPIFFE/SPIRE Core Architecture

SPIRE is the production-ready implementation of the SPIFFE specification [4]. It
uses a two-component architecture: a Server that acts as the certificate
authority and trust anchor, and an Agent deployed per-node that handles
attestation and SVID issuance to local workloads [4].

Attestation occurs in two phases: node attestation first establishes the
identity of the node itself, followed by workload attestation that identifies
specific processes running on that node [4][23]. Node attestors support
Kubernetes Projected Service Account Tokens (PSAT), x509pop, join tokens, TPM
devid, and cloud provider APIs including AWS Instance Identity Documents, Azure
Managed Service Identity, and GCE instance metadata [4]. Workload attestors
query the kubelet or Docker daemon to match selectors against registration
entries [4].

SPIRE uses a plugin architecture that allows extensibility across attestors,
datastores, key managers, and upstream authorities [23].

## SVID Formats

X.509-SVIDs encode the SPIFFE ID as a URI Subject Alternative Name per RFC 5280.
Each certificate contains exactly one URI SAN, sets the cA field to false, uses
the digitalSignature key usage, and includes both serverAuth and clientAuth
Extended Key Usages [4].

JWT-SVIDs are JWS-signed tokens with required claims for subject (sub), audience
(aud), and expiration (exp). Nine signing algorithms are supported across the
RS, ES, and PS families [4].

Default TTLs are 1 hour for X.509 SVIDs and 24 hours for CAs. Rotation triggers
at approximately 50% of the TTL [10].

## Trust Model

A trust domain represents an identity namespace backed by an issuing authority
holding cryptographic keys [4]. The SPIFFE bundle is an RFC 7517 JWK Set
extended with spiffe_sequence and spiffe_refresh_hint fields for federation [4].

## SPIRE Controller Manager

The SPIRE Controller Manager is a Kubernetes controller that reconciles
registration entries declaratively. It exposes three CRDs: ClusterSPIFFEID,
ClusterFederatedTrustDomain, and ClusterStaticEntry. It runs as a sidecar to the
SPIRE Server, communicating over a Unix Domain Socket [5].

## ZTWIM Operator Architecture

ZTWIM is an OpenShift Day-2 operator that manages the full SPIRE deployment
stack [5]. It deploys and reconciles four components: SPIRE Server (as a
StatefulSet), SPIRE Agent (as a DaemonSet), SPIFFE CSI Driver (as a DaemonSet),
and OIDC Discovery Provider [5][12].

SPIFFE IDs follow the format `spiffe://<trust-domain>/ns/<namespace>/sa/<serviceAccount>` [3][9].

The datastore layer supports SQLite for development, PostgreSQL, and MySQL, with
connection pooling and automatic migration [5].

## Gaps and Limitations

1. The system comprises 8-10 interdependent components, creating significant
   operational surface area [7].
2. The datastore is identified as the biggest bottleneck in SPIRE deployments,
   particularly at scale [10].
3. Agent synchronization occurs every 5 seconds, which can generate substantial
   load on the server at scale [10].
